key_insight: Combining per-episode (episodic) context with a persistent world memory prevents curiosity-driven agents from getting trapped in local revisit loops, enabling robust exploration in complex photorealistic 3D environments.
problem_solved: Curiosity-based intrinsic rewards cause agents to repeatedly revisit forgotten states in long-horizon, sparse-reward 3D scenes, preventing meaningful coverage and learning; this paper stops spurious novelty by remembering both recent episode context and long-term visited regions.
method: Episodic context: track short-term visitation and prediction errors within an episode to avoid re-rewarding immediately revisited states.
Persistent world memory: maintain a cross-episode representation of visited locations (a persistent map or state buffer) to suppress false novelty across episodes.
Modulated curiosity: compute intrinsic rewards from prediction error but discount or mask errors when state novelty is explained by episodic or persistent memory, improving exploration efficiency.
impact: Provides a practical framework to make curiosity-driven RL work in photorealistic, long-horizon 3D tasks, improving sample efficiency and coverage—useful for embodied agents, simulation-to-real transfer, and long-term autonomous exploration.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: agent with two memory streams (episodic buffer vs persistent world map) showing how intrinsic reward is gated.
Line/bar chart: exploration coverage or cumulative extrinsic reward over time comparing baseline curiosity vs episodic+persistent approach.
Episode timeline: visualization of repeated visits being suppressed across episodes by the persistent memory.
Icon set: curiosity (spark), memory (stacked cards), 3D environment (room/scene) to quickly convey core concepts.
paper_title: Remember to be Curious: Episodic Context and Persistent Worlds for 3D Exploration
paper_authors: Lily Goli, Justin Kerr, Daniele Reda, Alec Jacobson, Andrea Tagliasacchi
